@rive-app/webgl2 2.39.1 — vendored, unmodified.

Source:   https://registry.npmjs.org/@rive-app/webgl2/-/webgl2-2.39.1.tgz
Upstream: https://github.com/rive-app/rive-wasm/tree/master/js
Files:    rive.js, rive.wasm

Vendored rather than fetched from a CDN so the homepage has no third-party
runtime dependency (the runtime's default WASM URL points at unpkg, and its
fallback at jsdelivr).

WHY webgl2 AND NOT canvas / canvas-lite
Both Canvas2D runtimes render this file's animated mesh incorrectly: the orb's
tentacle fringe is a 24×5 deformed mesh, and Canvas2D draws only the first row
band, clipping everything below it (verified at 2.39.1 — the clip lands exactly
on mesh row 1). The webgl2 runtime renders the full fringe correctly. The
tradeoff is that webgl2 needs a real WebGL2 context and draws nothing at all
without one, so the loader in index.html feature-detects WebGL2 first and keeps
the static mark when it is unavailable.

If a future release fixes Canvas2D mesh rendering, canvas-lite would save
~510KB gzipped — worth re-testing on upgrade.

To update: download the tarball above at the new version, copy rive.js and
rive.wasm here verbatim, bump the version in this file, and confirm the hero
still animates WITH ITS FRINGE INTACT (see design/orb/README.md).
